Article Title: AIIMS Delhi displays live population count of India: How does it get data on newly born babies?
Article Text:
AIIMS population display (Instagram)

A population clock, not a birth register

So why the number keeps changing

India's last completed population Census

​A population clock (Instagram)

What about babies born at AIIMS?

Why does the clock look so precise?

A digital clock is going viral in Delhi. Well, it’s not an ordinary clock. It’s a population counter clock which is displayed at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS Delhi). It has recently attracted attention online, with the number on the screen changing continuously and appearing to show India’s population growing every second. Now, this viral display has also raised an important question: if the number increases every few seconds, is AIIMS actually receiving information every time a baby is born somewhere in India?So the answer is NO.It’s a population clock and it is an estimate based on demographic data and population projections. It’s not a nationwide live birth-tracking system. The distinction is important because India does have official systems for recording births and deaths. These systems do not work like a real-time national counter.The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s National Health Profile identifies the Census, registration of vital events, population surveys, population projections and the Sample Registration System (SRS) among the sources used for demographic information.The Civil Registration System (CRS), maintained through the registration machinery of the government, is responsible for the continuous recording of vital events such as births and deaths. The Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner describes civil registration as the continuous, permanent and compulsory recording of the occurrence and characteristics of vital events.But this does not mean that a national population display receives an electronic notification every time a birth takes place in India.Now this is where population estimation comes in. A population clock takes a known or estimated population at a particular reference point and applies demographic rates to project how that population changes over time.If the estimated population is expected to rise by a certain number over a year, the annual change can be mathematically distributed across months, days, hours, minutes and seconds. A digital display can therefore make the number appear to be changing in real time.If the display increases by one, it does not necessarily mean that a particular baby has just been born somewhere in India. It represents a calculated movement in the estimated population total.India's last completed population Census was conducted in 2011, when the country's population was recorded at about 121.1 crore. The National Health Profile notes that India's population was projected to increase from 121.1 crore in 2011 to 152.2 crore by 2036, an increase of about 25% over 25 years.The United Nations follows a similar demographic approach. Its World Population Prospects 2024 provides population estimates and projections based on analyses of historical demographic trends for countries and territories around the world.The fact that the clock is located at AIIMS can easily create another misconception that AIIMS might somehow be using its maternity records to calculate India's population.Instead, births are recorded through the country's civil registration framework, while demographic agencies use registration data, surveys and statistical methods to understand population trends.That is perhaps the most fascinating part of the viral display.A computer can calculate an estimated population to several decimal places and refresh the display every second. That does not mean demographers know the exact number of people alive in India at that precise second.The changing digits are essentially a visualisation of a statistical model. It is similar to a countdown or a continuously updated financial index: the display can change every second even though the underlying information is based on data collected over a longer period.The viral AIIMS population clock is therefore best understood as a demographic awareness tool, not as a nationwide surveillance mechanism for births.India's population is certainly changing continuously. Babies are being born, people are dying and migration changes the distribution of people across regions. So, the next time the AIIMS population clock ticks upward, it does not mean that a computer has just received the birth certificate of another Indian baby.
Article Summary: A digital clock is going viral in Delhi. It’s a population counter clock which is displayed at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS Delhi) It has recently attracted attention online, with the number on the screen changing continuously. It has also raised an important question: is AIIMS actually receiving information every time a baby is born somewhere in India?

Article Title: Janmashtami lights up Antilia: Inside the Ambani family's Janmashtami celebration
Article Text: Antilia came alive with colour, devotion and festive cheer this week as the Ambani family celebrated Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna.Footage from the evening shows the family's signature blend of devotion, colour and festive joy, a celebration that, over the years, has become one of the most talked-about traditions in India's festival calendar.The evening carried all the markers of a Janmashtami night. Flower-laden interiors dripping with strings of white and pink blooms, a dance floor painted with intricate motifs, and family members dressed in richly embroidered traditional silhouettes, deep purples, sea-greens, and reds threaded with gold. Prayers were offered with folded hands and floral garlands, following the rituals associated with the festival, which commemorates Krishna's birth at midnight and is celebrated across India and among Hindu communities worldwide with fasting, devotional singing, and the reenactment of Krishna's childhood.What stood out most in the visuals was the warmth, the women in the family twirling with children on the dance floor, a toddler being lifted into a gentle embrace mid-celebration, and quieter moments of prayer tucked between the festivities. It was a reminder that behind the headlines about India's best-known business family lies a fairly universal scene of generations coming together, in their finest clothes, to mark a day that matters to them.At its heart, though, the footage captures a family pausing from their famously packed schedules to celebrate a shared faith together, surrounded by children, colour, and candlelight. For a country as religiously and culturally diverse as India, it's worth remembering that such festival scenes, however grand the setting, echo similar celebrations happening in millions of homes on the same night, where the essentials remain unchanged: prayer, family, sweets, and a bit of dancing until midnight.
Article Summary: Antilia came alive with colour, devotion and festive cheer this week. The Ambani family celebrated Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna. Footage from the evening shows the family's signature blend of devotion, colour and festive joy.

Article Title: SC rejects panel's plea for 6 more months to define Aravali hills & ranges
Article Text:
SC rejects panel’s plea for 6 more months to define Aravali hills & ranges

NEW DELHI: "Why don't you simply say that the matter be heard after my retirement," asked an exasperated CJI Surya Kant as a bench led by him outrightly declined a request from the high-powered committee for six more months' time to draft a comprehensive definition of Aravali hills and ranges to protect the eco-sensitive area from mining and various commercial activities and fixed a Nov 30 deadline for submission of the final report.Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for HPC, told a bench of CJI, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that HPC would need six more months to file a detailed report, which would include completing public hearings and considering views of stakeholders. CJI Kant is to retire on Feb 9. A bench led by him had stayed the operation of SC's Nov 20 judgement accepting a very liberal definition of Aravali that had caused an uproar among environmentalists.
Article Summary: SC rejects panel’s plea for 6 more months to define Aravali hills & ranges. CJI Surya Kant is to retire on Feb 9. A bench led by him had stayed the operation of SC's Nov 20 judgement accepting a very liberal definition.

Article Title: National film awards ceremony to be in Gujarat this year
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A film on the Statue of Unity will be honoured in the shadow of the monument itself when the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony takes place at Ekta Nagar, formerly Kevadia, in Gujarat September 22.Govt has not spelt out the reason for shifting the ceremony out of New Delhi or indicated whether taking the awards to different locations will become a regular practice. The move nevertheless breaks with a long-established pattern. Instituted in 1954, the awards have overwhelmingly been presented in Delhi although University Centenary Auditorium in Madras, now Chennai, hosted the 17th chapter on November 21, 1970.Among those being honoured is filmmaker Aanand L Rai , who won Best Direction in the non-feature category for Statue of Unity - Ekta ka Prateek.
Article Summary: A film on the Statue of Unity will be honoured in the shadow of the monument itself. The 72nd National Film Awards ceremony takes place at Ekta Nagar, formerly Kevadia, in Gujarat September 22. Govt has not spelt out the reason for shifting the ceremony out of New Delhi.

Article Title: CM Omar Abdullah opens first J&K film fest, seeks to reclaim Kashmir's place in Indian cinema
Article Text:
Omar opens first J&K film fest, seeks to reclaim Kashmir’s place in Indian cinema

SRINAGAR: CM Omar Abdullah inaugurated the maiden edition of the International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) on Monday evening, calling it a new chapter in the region’s enduring relationship with cinema. Reminding filmmakers across the country that Kashmir had long been a destination for cinema, much before Switzerland and other international locations became popular, Omar said, “We would like that trend to start again.”Filmmaker Vidhu Vinod Chopra , who grew up and studied in Srinagar, said IFFJK was an emotional homecoming for him. He urged young and aspiring Kashmiri filmmakers to “show the world what you can do”. For actor Fatima Sana Shaikh, whose mother is from Kashmir, returning to the Valley after many years has brought back childhood memories.Filmmakers from 30 countries are participating in the four-day (Sept 7-10) event, with more than 130 movies being showcased. The IFFJK has brought together an eminent jury comprising Santosh Sivan, Dorothee Wenner, Keiko Bang and Himansu Sekhar Khatua.
Article Summary: CM Omar Abdullah inaugurated the maiden edition of the International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) on Monday evening. More than 130 movies from 30 countries are being showcased at the four-day event. The IFFJK has brought together an eminent jury comprising Santosh Sivan, Dorothee Wenner and Keiko Bang.

Article Title: Malaysia Airlines flight, with 186 passengers onboard, diverts to Chennai after engine snag
Article Text:
Malaysia Airlines' MH156 diverted to Chennai due to issue involving Engine No 2.

Emergency teams put on standby

Air India Express flight also diverted

NEW DELHI: A Malaysia Airlines flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jeddah was diverted to Chennai on Monday after a technical issue involving one of its engines, with a full emergency declared at the airport before the aircraft landed safely.Malaysia Airlines flight MH 156 was carrying 186 people when it was diverted. The aircraft landed safely and the airport activated the necessary emergency response arrangements.The technical problem involved "Engine No.2", an airport official said."Further assessment of the aircraft and the technical issue is being carried out by the airline and relevant technical teams," the spokesperson said, adding operations are normal.The aircraft was later moved to a parking bay using a tow vehicle, while the passengers were provided accommodation at the airport.Following the diversion, the relevant airport operational and emergency agencies were alerted and arrangements were made to handle the aircraft's arrival safely.The aircraft landed without any untoward incident. The airline's technical teams are now assessing the reported engine issue.Airport operations continued normally after the aircraft was brought to the parking area.Separately, an Air India Express flight from Tiruchirappalli to Singapore was also diverted to Chennai on Monday following a technical issue.A "local standby was declared" at Chennai airport and emergency response arrangements were kept ready.The aircraft landed safely and vacated the runway on its own power. The airline's engineering and technical team is assessing the issue."All operations are normal," the official added.
Article Summary: Malaysia Airlines flight MH 156 was carrying 186 people when it was diverted. The technical problem involved "Engine No.2", an airport official said. Air India Express flight from Tiruchirappalli to Singapore was also diverted to Chennai.

Article Title: Hailee Steinfeld’s latest career move catches Josh Allen’s attention as Beau Society expands into a new venture
Article Text:
Hailee Steinfeld and Josh Allen (Image via Getty Images)

Hailee Steinfeld expands Beau Society with new merch

Josh Allen shows support for Hailee Steinfeld’s latest move

Hailee Steinfeld has found a new way to turn a personal passion into a growing brand, and Josh Allen is quietly cheering her on. The actress and Buffalo Bills quarterback’s wife has expanded Beau Society beyond her newsletter with a limited merchandise drop. Allen did not need a long public message to show his support. One Instagram Story was enough to get fans talking.Steinfeld’s Beau Society has become more than a newsletter. After reaching its 100th issue on August 28, the actress celebrated the milestone before giving subscribers another reason to pay attention.The latest move is a small clothing collection tied directly to the Beau Society identity. The first drop includes the Beau Society Tee, the “This is BS” hat and the Beau tee.The launch arrived Saturday, with the Beau Society Instagram account sharing photographs of Steinfeld wearing pieces from the collection. Rather than keeping the announcement limited to her own platform, Steinfeld also encouraged readers of her newsletter to check out the limited-edition release.“Surprise! Beau Society merch out now!” read the caption of the post.Steinfeld later described the collection as a limited-edition drop, adding a sense of urgency for followers who want to buy something from the first release."As always, this is a limited-edition drop, so get it while it’s hot," Steinfeld wrote in the 101st issue of her newsletter on Saturday.The move also shows how Beau Society is evolving. What began as a newsletter has developed into a recognizable personal brand, giving Steinfeld a space to connect with followers outside her acting career.Allen’s contribution to the launch was far less flashy, but it still caught attention.The Bills quarterback shared the Beau Society merchandise post on his Instagram Story. There was no lengthy caption or elaborate announcement from Allen. He simply amplified his wife’s new project to his own audience.That low-key gesture fits the way the couple has often shared glimpses of their life while keeping much of it private.Steinfeld recently marked another personal milestone when she reached 100 issues of Beau Society. In that edition, she opened up about the celebration and shared a warm family moment.“I’m writing this issue from a barstool at my kitchen island,” Steinfeld wrote. “Beside me is the most beautiful bouquet my family sent me and my breakfast: a big piece of funfetti cake with pink frosting. I don’t know why, but cake for breakfast seems like the perfect way to ring in Beau Society’s 100th issue!”The couple has also spoken about their life as parents. Allen previously revealed that he and Steinfeld have developed a simple nighttime tradition after their daughter goes to sleep.“We’re trying to limit the screens ‘cause if there’s a screen, she’s over there looking,” Allen said. “When we know that [her] eyes are closed and almost out, my wife and I play the New York Times crossword every night. That’s our little routine that we love doing.”For Steinfeld, Beau Society now appears to be entering another chapter. And with Allen quietly backing her latest venture, the project has plenty of personal meaning behind it.
Article Summary: Hailee Steinfeld has expanded Beau Society with a limited merchandise drop. The actress and Buffalo Bills quarterback’s wife has expanded her newsletter into a brand. Allen did not need a long public message to show his support. He simply amplified his wife's new project to his own audience.

Article Title: 'I was disrespected and undermined': Former Pakistan coach drops bombshell, names 'untouchable' figure behind England tour mess
Article Text:
Aaqib Javed, Jason Gillespie

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) consider changing their selection process? Yes, immediate changes are needed. No, the current process is fine. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Former Pakistan head coach Jason Gillespie has doubled down on his criticism of Pakistan chief selector Aaqib Javed , saying the selection committee chairman took control of Pakistan cricket and changed the direction the team was supposed to follow.Gillespie, who was appointed Pakistan's head coach in April 2024 and resigned in December that year, said he was brought in with a clear vision of rebuilding Pakistan's fast-bowling culture. According to him, that plan changed after Javed became the chief selector.“When I came on board, they wanted to bring back fast bowling,” Gillespie said, while talking to UK-based outlet The Telegraph. “This is what was sold to me when I took on the role. They wanted to prepare surfaces that would bounce and carry and would encourage fast bowling because they felt that fast bowling was dying. I was on board and thought: ‘This is going to be really cool.’"“The appointment of Javed fundamentally altered the landscape,” he adds. “From that moment, my relationship with Pakistan cricket completely changed. Aaqib came in and took over. It appeared to me that he was in charge of absolutely everything."Gillespie's comments come after Pakistan made drastic changes during their ongoing tour of England. Following defeats in the first two Tests at Headingley and Lord's, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) sent seven players home, removed Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul, and appointed Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke for the third and final Test in Birmingham starting September 9.There have also been reports that the PCB confiscated the phones of some players in England as part of an inquiry into the team's "discipline and conduct" during the tour.Senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha were among the players sent back to Pakistan before Hesson joined the squad. Fast bowler Khurram Shahzad and spinner Ali Usman, who featured in both Tests, were also released, while all-rounder Aamir Jamal and batter Mohammad Awais returned home without playing a match.Meanwhile, Gillespie said working under Javed left him feeling sidelined and disrespected.“I was totally disrespected and undermined and I direct that towards Aaqib Javed. At our first meeting he came in with bravado, bluff, and bluster, wanting to show he was the man in charge. He said: ‘This is what we need to do.’ I listened and said OK. But this kept on happening and I pushed back on a couple of his comments. I just felt from that moment on that it wasn’t going to work because he’d already decided what he was going to do. There was going to be no collaboration whatsoever," Gillespie added.The former Australia fast bowler said Javed had the backing of the PCB chairman and the board, which made him feel untouchable.“Aaqib had the support of the chairman and the board and that’s why he felt he was untouchable,” Gillespie says. “As a coach, you feel compromised. He was not a collaborative chairman of selectors. He doesn’t take on other people’s ideas, thoughts, or opinions. He might think he does, but he doesn’t. It was his way or the highway."Gillespie also claimed the PCB still owes him money from his time as coach but said he was not willing to change his principles to stay in the job.“The PCB still owes me thousands of dollars, but I was never going to be a yes man,” he says. “I wasn’t going to compromise on my principles, I never have throughout my career and I certainly wasn’t going to change.I could have stayed quiet, agreed to everything and taken home my salary, but that’s not me and part of me knew I was probably going to be sacked in a couple of months anyway.”Gillespie said Pakistan cricket remains trapped in a damaging cycle and lays the blame at the feet of Javed.“It’s heartbreaking for me to see what’s going on now, it’s a mess,” Gillespie said, as quoted by Telegraph. “I know the crux of it. It’s Aaqib Javed. He is the problem and as long as he is there, then Pakistan cricket will continue to go backwards," the former Pakistan coach said.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan head coach Jason Gillespie has doubled down on his criticism of Pakistan chief selector Aaqib Javed. Gillespie said he was brought in with a clear vision of rebuilding Pakistan's fast-bowling culture. According to him, that plan changed after Javed became the chief selector. Gillespie also claimed the PCB still owes him money from his time as coach.

Article Title: Who is Carly Korwin? Spencer Korwin’s widow reveals ‘worst day’ after former Team USA triathlete’s tragic drowning
Article Text:
Who is Carly Korwin? Spencer Korwin’s widow reveals ‘worst day’ after former Team USA triathlete’s tragic drowning

Who is Carly Korwin, Spencer Korwin’s widow?

What happened to Spencer Korwin on Shelter Island?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Team USA triathlete Spencer Korwin’s widow Carly Korwin broke down in tears while remembering her husband at his funeral in New York on Sunday. Spencer, 38, died after drowning during a family vacation on Shelter Island on September 2. His body was found beneath the dock at The Pridwin Hotel several hours after he went missing during a morning swim. Carly spoke about their marriage, their two young daughters and the life they had built together. She called Spencer the love of her life and said she still could not accept that he was gone. The funeral was held at Temple Israel.Carly Korwin, née Shapiro, is Spencer Korwin’s widow. She is a Syracuse University graduate and works in advertising and marketing in New York City. Carly and Spencer reconnected and began dating years after college before getting married. They lived in Manhattan and had two daughters, Sadie, 4, and Colette, 1.Carly became the focus of attention after giving an emotional eulogy for Spencer. Speaking through tears, she said, “This is a nightmare. This is the worst day of my life. I can’t accept that this is real and that Spencer is not going to come home.”She then spoke about the man he was to her and their children.“Spencer was more than I could ever have dreamed of when it came to a husband, a father, and a friend. He was the best human I have ever met, and he was the love of my life.“We had the most beautiful and special once-in-a-lifetime type of love, and we knew it.“We always said forever isn’t long enough. And I will never be able to make sense as to why this incredible life we built together, filled with happiness and so much love, was ripped away from us in an instant.”Carly also remembered the small things Spencer did for his family. “He wrote me and the girls notes all the time and hung them around the apartment,” she said.“He was filled with surprises and hugs just because… he had automated texts set up twice a day just to remind me that he loves me, I’m a wonderful mom and wife.“I know the girls will never stop missing him, and he will forever be their hero.”Spencer was on vacation with Carly and their daughters when he went into the water near the hotel dock at about 8 a.m. on September 2. When he did not return, Carly alerted hotel staff, who contacted emergency services. A search involving marine and air units followed, and divers found his body underwater near the dock around 3 p.m.The Shelter Island Police Department said the death is believed to be accidental, while the official cause remains pending the medical examiner’s report. Police also said the waters can have strong currents because of the narrow passage and that tides and boat traffic are always factors.Spencer was a Syracuse University graduate and represented Team USA at the 2012 Triathlon World Championship in Auckland, New Zealand. He later moved into health and wellness, founding Korwin Health & Wellness in 2021 and previously working as a trainer for SportsLab NYC.The details of Carly’s tribute were reported by the Daily Mail, while local authorities and other reports have confirmed the circumstances surrounding Spencer’s death.
Article Summary: Spencer Korwin, 38, died after drowning during a family vacation on Shelter Island on September 2. His body was found beneath the dock at The Pridwin Hotel several hours after he went missing during a morning swim. Spencer represented Team USA at the 2012 Triathlon World Championship in Auckland, New Zealand.

Article Title: Alex Eala could face heavy WTA punishment after choosing Philippines at Asian Games over China Open
Article Text:
Alex Eala reveals surprising dating red flags before US Open as she opens up about what instantly turns her off

Eala chooses Asian Games over China Open

Alexandra Eala (AP Photo)

PHILTA asks WTA to protect Eala from punishment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Alex Eala could face a fine and ranking consequences after choosing to represent the Philippines at the Asian Games instead of competing at the China Open, although her federation has formally asked the WTA to grant her an exemption.The decision comes after Eala's impressive run at the 2026 US Open, where she reached the third round before losing to American teenager Iva Jovic at Arthur Ashe Stadium. She has now confirmed that her next tournament will be the Singapore Tennis Open, before she heads to Japan to represent the Philippines at the Asian Games.Eala explained after her US Open defeat that the opportunity to compete for her country was too important to pass up.Speaking to the media after her loss to Jovic, Eala confirmed that she expects to play in Singapore before joining the Philippine team at the Asian Games.“Yes, before (Asian Games) I believe, I will be in Singapore,” Eala said, via Tennis Head.“But yeah, I love playing and competing with the Philippines team and in the SEA, the Asian Games I've also done, I think it's a really fun environment, I love being with the team.”Eala added: “Especially this last SEA Games in December, I had such a great time and I think they're really memories that will stick with me.“You know, the Asian Games happens once every four years and yeah, I just found myself drawn to compete in that over other stuff.”That commitment means Eala will miss the 2026 China Open in Beijing, which is scheduled to take place later this month at around the same time as the Asian Games.According to the Daily Tribune , Eala is one of only two players inside the women's top 20 rankings who will miss the China Open, with world No.15 Victoria Mboko currently sidelined by injury.Eala's decision could therefore leave her facing potential punishment from the WTA.According to Tennis365 , the China Open is a WTA 1000 event, making it one of the tournaments regarded as mandatory for players ranked high enough to qualify. The WTA's rules allow players to miss mandatory events in certain circumstances, including injury, other medical issues and personal reasons.Players who miss such an event without an applicable exemption can receive zero ranking points for the tournament. The effect on Eala's ranking, however, would depend partly on how other players perform at the US Open and Singapore Open.She could also face a $10,000 fine, according to the WTA's 2026 rulebook. That is the reported late-withdrawal fine for players ranked between 11th and 25th.Whether the Asian Games will qualify Eala for an exemption remains unclear.The Philippine Tennis Association (PHILTA) has already formally approached the WTA over the matter, requesting that Eala be exempted from the penalties because she will be representing her country.PHILTA secretary-general John Tiangco, who is also the mayor of Navotas City, confirmed the request to GMA Network. “We have formally informed the WTA that Alex will be representing the Philippines at the Asian Games and have requested an exemption so she will not be penalized for missing a WTA 1000 event,” Tiangco said.“Alex herself has made it clear that representing the Philippines is an honor and that she is choosing to play for the flag,” he added.“We fully support that decision and are doing everything we can to ensure that choosing to represent her country does not come at the expense of her standing on the WTA Tour.”Eala has plenty of experience representing the Philippines on the international stage. She is a two-time Asian Games bronze medallist, having finished third in both the women's singles and mixed doubles, and she won gold in the women's singles at the 2025 Southeast Asian Games in Thailand.Her decision comes during the best period of her professional career so far.Eala won her first WTA singles title in Washington D.C. in August and has climbed to a career-high No.18 in the world rankings. Her run at the US Open was also her best finish at the tournament, with her campaign ending against Jovic in the third round.Her rapid rise has made Eala one of the biggest emerging names in women's tennis, with her US Open appearance even contributing to a significant surge in ticket prices as fans rushed to watch the Filipina compete on one of the sport's biggest stages.The China Open would have offered another major opportunity, with the WTA 1000 event carrying valuable ranking points and bringing together many of the world's leading players.Instead, Eala has chosen the Asian Games.The decision now rests with the WTA, which will determine whether her commitment to representing the Philippines provides sufficient grounds for an exemption from the penalties associated with missing the mandatory Beijing tournament.
Article Summary: Alex Eala could face a fine and ranking consequences after choosing to represent the Philippines at the Asian Games instead of competing at the China Open. The decision comes after Eala's impressive run at the 2026 US Open, where she reached the third round before losing to American teenager Iva Jovic. She has now confirmed that her next tournament will be the Singapore Tennis Open, before she heads to Japan. The Philippine Tennis Association has formally asked the WTA to grant her an exemption.

Article Title: Duleep Trophy final: Ishan Kishan signals red-ball intent with mammoth 270
Article Text:
East Zone's captain Ishan Kishan plays a shot on day 2 of the Duleep Trophy 2026-27 final cricket match between South Zone and East Zone, in Chennai. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: Ishan Kishan has developed a habit of saving his best for the big occasion. Last year, he led Jharkhand to the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy title and produced a match-winning century in the final, a performance that helped him earn his way back into India's T20I setup. After playing a matchwinning hand against Pakistan in Colombo in the T20 World Cup earlier in the year, Kishan delivered again in the Duleep final on Monday, leading East Zone against South at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.Kishan smashed 270 off 334 balls (30x4, 7x6), taking East to a mammoth 708 all out, Kumar Kushagra chipping in with 101 as well. The double century, his second in first-class cricket, came after a gap of 10 years and has further strengthened his case for a return to India's red-ball setup.A triple century seemed on the cards after he crossed 250, but Kishan said that personal landmarks never occupied his mind. Interestingly, he himself was unaware that it had been 10 years since he scored a first-class double century. "Honestly, I wasn't even thinking about 50, forget 300. I was only thinking about 50-run partnerships," Kishan said.The double century came off 273 balls. He then accelerated dramatically, reaching 250 in only 27 more balls.But the intent, he said, was never to chase numbers. "I didn't change anything in my game plan. I was just batting normally. Once I got set, my thought was not to throw my wicket away. I have enough confidence in my shots to know that if I play well, I will either clear the field or find the gap," he said.For Kishan, the most satisfying aspect of the innings was the temperament he showed. With East having won the toss and opted to bat, the priority was to build a total that would put South under pressure. "I would rate this innings very highly because I kept the team's goal ahead of my own runs. There were moments when I could have played more attacking shots, but the priority was to spend time in the middle, make good decisions and build a big total," he said.That approach was shaped by a mindset Kishan believes has changed considerably during his time away from the Indian team. Having spent to two years grinding it out in domestic cricket, he said the experience taught him to simplify his game. "When you're playing for India regularly, sometimes you get into a flow and your growth can stagnate. Going back to domestic cricket makes you start from zero. You realise there are so many players scoring runs and that you have to perform better to get back," he said.
Article Summary: East Zone captain Ishan Kishan scores double century in Duleep Trophy final. The 270 came off 334 balls (30x4, 7x6), taking East to a mammoth 708 all out. Kumar Kushagra chipped in with 101 as well. The double century came after a gap of 10 years.

Article Title: Carlos Alcaraz gets into groove, beats local favourite Tommy Paul to reach US Open quarterfinals
Article Text:
Carlos Alcaraz

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW YORK CITY: There was a moment early in the US Open fourth-round match when Tommy Paul was pulled wide, he lunged forward and, out of nowhere, slammed a forehand winner around the post, landing it behind a stunned Carlos Alcaraz. The crowd gasped, and a flicker of a smile crossed Paul's face. That was the kind of tennis the 29-year-old needed to produce just to make the match competitive against the defending champion.Instead, it was Alcaraz's forehand that lit up Arthur Ashe. The Spaniard ripped it from just about anywhere on the court, threading the needle and neutralising the American's serve as much through positioning as timing. The second seed finished with 33 winners, 17 of them off the forehand side.The world No. 3, returning from a four-month injury-enforced break, advanced to the quarter-finals with a statement 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 win, having dropped just one set across four matches.Sunday was the pair's ninth meeting, with Alcaraz now leading the head-to-head 7-2. Paul, the world No. 21, had won two of their first three meetings back in 2022-23, but on Sunday he admitted he was nowhere near the level required."It sucks! It felt like he's playing at a completely different level than me.It sucks, because you feel like, sh@#t!" Paul said. "But at the same time, you learn a lot every time you play him. Every time I've played him, we've gone to the practice court with new ideas of what he does well and what I can try and put into my game."The practice court had also played a part in Alcaraz's own turnaround in the first week.After his third-round win over China's Yibing Wu, in which he had managed just nine winners off his forehand while making 19 unforced errors on the same side, the Spaniard went back to work."For a tennis player, it's really important how you go to bed in terms of feeling. Especially when you win the match, but you don't feel like you've been hitting the ball well, it is better to go back to the practice court and then just hit for five-ten minutes. Just to hit some balls when you're not nervous or you're not thinking about anything else. Leave the site with a good feeling."Alcaraz left Flushing Meadows feeling a lot better about his forehand on Friday."I think everybody saw the difference in my forehand today," he said.The 23-year-old, who exchanged his espresso-brown gear for a black-and-white look, also noted that his Grand Slam off-days now look very different from previous years.Golf had been his favourite escape when he wanted to get away from the pressure of the tennis court. But after the wrist injury, he cannot risk putting his wrist through the demands of the game. These days, his downtime is about recovery and preparing for the next round.Alcaraz will play the eighth-seeded American Ben Shelton next in the last-eight on Tuesday. The 23-year-old moved past Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 and is into his sixth major quarter-final and his second at Flushing Meadows, where he made the semi-finals in 2023.Meanwhile, Frances Tiafoe shocked 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (1), 6-4, 7-6 (6) to earn one of his biggest wins of the season.The 28-year-old world No. 12, roared on by the home crowd, was pumped up for his clash on Louis Armstrong Stadium as he reached the quarter-finals in New York for the fourth time.The two-time US Open semifinalist had lost six of his previous seven meetings with Medvedev, but was the sharper and more focused of the two through the two-hour, 57-minute contest. Tiafoe will face compatriot Alex Michelsen in the last-eight.
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz beats Tommy Paul to reach US Open quarter-finals. World No. 3 returns from four-month injury-enforced break. Frances Tiafoe shocks 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev to reach last eight.

Article Title: Jasprit Bumrah will hold key to NZ series, says Mitchell Santner
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah

How crucial will it be for India to adapt to conditions given only a few players from the current set-up have played Tests in NZ?

What's your take on India's pace attack?

Did you have a look at Manav Suthar?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What do you think about India's struggles in Test cricket recently?

How important is ETPL for the European players, who don't always get to play a lot of top-quality cricket?

CHENNAI: The road to the World Test Championship (WTC) final for India is getting tougher, with every series carrying greater significance. The task has become even more challenging after they failed to win the final Test against Sri Lanka recently.India's next step takes them to New Zealand for a two-Test series, having not won there in a decade and a half. NZ's premier left-arm spinner Mitchell Santner , who is leading Edinburgh Castle Rockers in the ongoing European T20 Premier League (ETPL), told TOI in an exclusive chat that India's pace attack, led by Jasprit Bumrah , will play a major role in the final outcome of the series. Excerpts...The first thing is to try and understand the conditions as quickly as possible. A few players have been there before and done well. In Oct-Nov, the pitches can play differently compared to Feb-March. So, early in the season in New Zealand, the ball might move around a little bit. It is about getting your head around that.Bumrah leading the attack and being able to nip and swing the ball will hold the key. (Mohammed) Siraj has done it for a long time as well and (Prasidh) Krishna is obviously bowling well.There is a lot of variety, which is what you need.He has been very impressive since he made his debut. He gets nice and tight to the stumps and gets good shape on the ball. He does bowl with good overspin when he needs to and that is the key in NZ, trying to get a bit of bounce especially if there is grass. I think there is still a role for a spinner in NZ, especially in Tests alongside the quicks, whether it is first or second innings when the pitch might be holding up.On days four and five, it could spin a bit. Whether it is Jadeja or Suthar, both are very good options.I think it has always been a challenge. They always play the best teams, and then having to adapt to the conditions quickly is the main thing. But they have got all bases covered.It is perfect for Scottish, Irish and players from Holland. It gives them more exposure and opportunity to play against some good players. We have seen how good they are in their own right. To be fair, in the last few years, we have had some great games against Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands. You throw a few overseas players in, and the tournament (ETPL) is really strong.There is some great cricket on show already, which is good. And we are only halfway through.
Article Summary: India's next step takes them to New Zealand for a two-Test series, having not won there in a decade and a half. NZ's premier left-arm spinner Mitchell Santner told TOI in an exclusive chat that India's pace attack, led by Jasprit Bumrah, will play a major role in the final outcome.

Article Title: Picking Bumrah for Asian Games is a good idea: Sunil Gavaskar
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'Asian Games title defence won't be easy'

(This interaction was facilitated by Sony Sports Network)

Bengaluru: The BCCI's decision to send a full-strength squad to the Asian Games later this month has brought one name into focus - Jasprit Bumrah. The premier India pacer has not played for India since the second ODI against England in Cardiff in July, when he limped off after suffering an impact injury to his left knee. He has since been undergoing rehabilitation and is part of India's squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, although his participation is subject to fitness clearance.With the Asian Games in Japan beginning later this month, former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes the tournament could provide Bumrah with valuable game time ahead of India's next major assignment, the New Zealand tour.The Asian Games, then, is the perfect opportunity for Bumrah to ease back into competitive cricket before that series. "There's a fair gap between the Asian Games and the New Zealand series, so playing Bumrah in the Asian Games is actually a good idea because he has to get some bowling under his belt. In Sri Lanka, we heard Mohammad Siraj was not quite in rhythm because he hadn't played enough in competitive matches. The bowlers need to get some overs and Bumrah getting them is very essential," Gavaskar said.Although Shreyas Iyer has lost six of the seven T20Is he has led India in this year, Sunil Gavaskar backed him. "He's very experienced as a captain, having led Kolkata Knight Riders, Delhi Capitals and Punjab Kings. I don't think there should be any pressure on him at the Asian Games. "Gavaskar was quick to add that the title defence won't be an easy ride for India. "It's going to be tough because it's a T20 tournament. Bangladesh are in form, Pakistan are always dangerous and Sri Lanka are a terrific team, not to forget Afghanistan, so it's not going to be easy at all," he said. Gavaskar pointed out that the Asian Games will be a huge learning experience for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. "To be able to meet sportspersons from other sports from across Asia can be an absolute treat. For Sooryavanshi, I hope it turns out to be even more inspirational because he will get to rub shoulders with athletes who he's looked up to."
Article Summary: Jasprit Bumrah is part of India's squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan. The premier India pacer has not played for India since the second ODI against England in Cardiff in July. Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes the tournament could provide Bumra with valuable game time ahead of the New Zealand tour.

Article Title: ‘We’ll sacrifice points’: World No.1 Sabalenka fires warning at WTA, ATP to end mandatory events over brutal schedule
Article Text:
Aryna Sabalenka, of Belarus, reacts as she competes against Taylor Townsend, of the United States, during the fourth round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)

Sabalenka wants players to choose what is best for their health

Sabalenka could sacrifice ranking position despite No.1 milestone

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aryna Sabalenka has called on the WTA and ATP to scrap mandatory tournaments altogether, warning that players may have to sacrifice ranking points and positions if the increasingly demanding tennis calendar is not eased.The world No.1 joined Carlos Alcaraz in speaking out about the workload during the US Open, with the Spaniard revealing that he intends to start taking longer breaks and skipping tournaments rather than attempting to play every required event.Sabalenka went a step further, arguing that players should have greater control over their schedules so they can protect their bodies.The tennis calendar has become an increasingly contentious issue in recent years, with players facing mandatory commitments at WTA 1000 level as well as requirements to compete in WTA 500 events depending on their ranking and eligibility.There are 10 WTA 1000 tournaments on the 2026 calendar, several of which have been expanded to 12-day formats, adding to the number of weeks elite players are required to spend competing at the highest level.Missing mandatory tournaments can also carry financial and ranking-point consequences, making it harder for players to simply take time away from competition when they feel they need to recover.Alcaraz raised the issue after reaching the third round of the US Open, saying he wants to take more time away from the sport rather than allow the schedule to dictate his entire season.“I want to have the breaks that I need to prepare the tournaments, to have the time to prepare the tournaments, to miss the tennis, to miss the tour, to miss you guys,” Alcaraz said.“I think that’s really important.”The Spaniard, who was competing at his first tournament in four and a half months at the US Open, also made clear that he expects to miss more tournaments in the future.“In the future, I’m going to take some breaks, some long breaks,” Alcaraz said.“Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it’s impossible to play them all.”Sabalenka backed the sentiment but believes the solution should go further than simply allowing individual players to skip the occasional event.“I would love to see changes to the calendar and eliminate the mandatory events to let the players decide what's best for their health,” Sabalenka said.She acknowledged how difficult it is to maintain the intensity required at the top of the sport across such a long season.“It’s been incredibly intense. Especially if you play at the level Carlos plays, which is basically very consistent, it’s very hard on the body.”Sabalenka then issued a warning about what could happen if the tours refuse to reduce the demands.“If they’re not going to reduce it, we’ll have to sacrifice points, ranking position, whatever it takes, to protect our bodies,” she said.“I think it would be really helpful for the WTA and ATP to relax the calendar a bit for us in order to truly support our health.”The current structure requires top-ranked players to compete at the mandatory WTA 1000 events, while players can also have obligations at the WTA 500 level. On the men's side, Alcaraz faces a similarly packed schedule involving the mandatory Masters events and selected 500 tournaments.Sabalenka's comments come as she approaches a significant milestone at the top of the women's rankings.She has spent 99 consecutive weeks as world No.1, but reaching 100 weeks is not guaranteed.The Belarusian must successfully defend her US Open title to retain her position, while a strong run from Elena Rybakina could prevent her from extending her reign. Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff could also enter the race for the top ranking, depending on how far they progress at the final Grand Slam of the season.Despite the significance of the milestone, Sabalenka said she is trying not to become consumed by rankings projections or outside speculation.“I completely separate myself from that because it's just like guessing,” she said.“I'm just trying to bring my best tennis every time I'm competing out there and basically fight for it.”She added that social media constantly produces new statistics and predictions, but she prefers to stay away from them.“There's always different statistics that social media brings. So I'm just completely away trying to stay away from it.”For Sabalenka, the same principle applies to the possibility of losing the No.1 ranking.“The situation is under my control for now, so I'm just trying to control what I can,” she said.“When it's no longer in my hands, it will no longer be in my hands. Why would I even think about it?”
Article Summary: Aryna Sabalenka has called on the WTA and ATP to scrap mandatory tournaments altogether. The world No.1 warned that players may have to sacrifice ranking points and positions if the increasingly demanding tennis calendar is not eased. The tennis calendar has become an increasingly contentious issue in recent years.

Article Title: 'That was a pity': Viswanathan Anand after losing on time to Magnus Carlsen, who lauds India's 'love for chess'
Article Text:
Viswanathan Anand loses on time to Magnus Carlsen (GCL Photos)

What happened on Day 3 in GCL

Team Played Won Drawn Lost Match Points Game Points 1 APL Pipers 4 3 0 1 9 43 2 Mumba Masters 4 2 0 2 6 36 3 American Gambits 4 2 0 2 6 34 4 Alaskan Knights 4 2 0 2 6 30 5 Ganges Grandmasters 4 1 0 3 3 28 6 Triveni Continental Kings 4 1 0 3 3 34

GCL 2026 : Schedule for Day 4, Tuesday, September 8

BENGALURU: The fast-paced world of chess has seen many terms evolve over time. “Flagging” is one of them. It generally refers to winning a game purely on time when an opponent’s clock hits 0:00, regardless of the evaluation on the board. From the perspective of both players and spectators, it’s a tense, chaotic climax where speed outruns strategy.On Monday, that exact high-wire drama took centre stage during the Day 3 marquee clash between APL Pipers' Magnus Carlsen and Alaskan Knights' Viswanathan Anand on the icon board. With seconds ticking down in a sharp middle-game battle, Anand failed to hit his clock in time, allowing Carlsen to snatch a win on time."A few moves ago, I had a few seconds more than him, so somehow my brain stopped looking at the clock, and I didn't keep one second left,” Anand told reporters after the opening match of the day. "Once I make a move, I will get some time, but apparently I let my clock run out. That was a pity, but I'm happy the team won."Despite losing his game, Anand’s squad pulled off the overall match victory. "I'm not happy with my play, but at least it didn't cost us," the five-time world champion added.The current World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen also gave his side of the dramatic finish against his longtime rival."I felt like I was playing him a little bit in the middle game.I was pretty happy with the position from the opening, and then again I was a little bit shaky with little time,” Carlsen stated.“For a period there, he was defending very, very well, not making it any worse, and then I just obviously resigned myself to a draw. Then I randomly glanced at his clock and saw that it was out. That's how it goes sometimes at times like this."Later, in Pipers’ game against the Gambits, Carlsen also raised eyebrows by uncorking 3...f6 against World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov, before holding him to a draw.Explaining the unexpected move, Carlsen added, "It (the idea) was originally from my coach. It was a misclick, and then he started looking at it. I kind of like the general idea of taking kind of a random move in the opening, and then with computer analysis, you can make pretty much anything work. The main idea is that after castles, a6, it's actually already not terrible."Despite his self-described "underwhelming" form, Carlsen expressed deep appreciation for the crowd in Bengaluru, saying, "It's very nice to play here. Chess in India is massive. That's great to see, and I definitely want to come here and experience the love people have for chess."Day 3 saw intense action across four team face-offs. Alaskan Knights edged past Alpine APL Pipers 9–7 in the first match of the day, but the Pipers stormed back later in with a commanding, one-sided 15–3 win over American Gambits. Meanwhile, Mumba Masters dominated Ganges Grandmasters 12–3, while Triveni Continental Kings secured an 11–6 victory, their first in the tournament, over Alaskan Knights in the final match of the day.Following the Day 3 results, APL Pipers hold top spot with 9 match points, closely followed by Mumba Masters, American Gambits, and Alaskan Knights tied at 6 points each. Ganges Grandmasters and Triveni Continental Kings round out the bottom of the table with 3 match points apiece.3.30 PM: Ganges Grandmasters vs Alaskan Knights5.00 PM: American Gambits vs Mumba Masters6.30 PM: Triveni Continental Kings vs APL Pipers8.00 PM: American Gambits vs Alaskan Knights

Article Title: Ollie Millroy’s wife Fern Millroy gives graphic update on British racing driver from hospital after his Ferrari’s horror crash during China GT race
Article Text:
Ollie Millroy crash (via X)

Fern Millroy reveals Ollie Millroy’s injuries after terrifying fireball crash

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

British racing driver Ollie Millroy remains in hospital in Shanghai after suffering serious injuries in a horror crash during a China GT event. His wife, Fern Millroy, has now revealed the extent of his injuries following surgery.Fern said the operation went well but revealed that Ollie still needs high-flow oxygen as his lung recovers. She also admitted she “can’t believe” he survived the terrifying incident, while praising fellow driver Loek Hartog for helping pull him from the burning Ferrari.Ollie Millroy was involved in a horrific accident at the Shanghai International Circuit during a China GT race. His Ferrari was hit after two other cars collided and spun across the track.The impact caused Ollie’s car to instantly burst into flames. He became trapped inside the Ferrari as the vehicle was engulfed by fire.Loek Hartog, who was also competing in the event, immediately rushed to help. New footage shows the 23-year-old driver desperately searching through the remains of the Ferrari to free Millroy.Ollie later underwent surgery at a hospital in Shanghai.His wife Fern has remained by his side throughout the ordeal.She provided a detailed update on his condition after the operation.She wrote on her Instagram stories, “Surgery went well yesterday, it took several hours, main work being his right hand. He now has metal along the entirety of his clavicle right side, metal inside his right hand, six broken ribs supported with a compression wrap and on high flow oxygen whilst his lung recovers.“Tried to come off the oxygen but his O2 level was just too low. He is in great care at this fantastic hospital in Shanghai and we can’t thank the staff here enough. More X Rays and CT tomorrow morning”, she continued.Fern also highlighted the crucial role played by Hartog. She added, “I still can’t believe he’s alive, purely down to our real life superhero Loek Hartog.”Loek Hartog has also spoken about the support surrounding the incident. He thanked people for their messages before travelling back home.He wrote, “Overwhelmed by the support from everyone over the past two days. I feel incredibly lucky to be part of a racing community that looks after each other the way this one does.”He also thanked everyone for all the messages and support that fans sent to Ollie, his wife and family, and also to him and his family. He revealed that he’s travelling back home now and can’t wait to be there. He also mentioned that he’s feeling good for now, but there have naturally been a lot of thoughts running through his head over the past few days.Notably, Fern and Ollie have been married since 2021 and have three young children. The family is now supporting Ollie as he continues his recovery in hospital.The racing community has also offered support to the British driver and Hartog following the frightening crash.

His Ferrari was hit after two other cars collided and spun across the track. The impact caused Ollie’s car to instantly burst into flames. Article Title: Take it or leave it: Across Delhi, they put lives on line to study
Article Text:
In areas like Laxmi Nagar and adjoining Shakarpur and West Angad Nagar, PGs and rented rooms have proliferated around coaching centres.

Satya Niketan building collapse





NEW DELHI: In Delhi’s student hubs, finding a PG accommodation can mean squeezing through cramped lanes and narrow staircases in tightly-packed buildings.“PG available” signs compete with tangled wires and exposed meters. In some pockets, dug-up approach roads and poor ventilation add to the worry. Yet, students pay steep rents for small rooms simply to stay close to college and coaching centres.The building collapse in Satya Niketan has renewed concerns over safety in the city’s student and coaching hubs, where many students depend on private accommodation.In areas like Laxmi Nagar and adjoining Shakarpur and West Angad Nagar, PGs and rented rooms have proliferated around coaching centres. Some buildings stand along narrow, uneven or excavated stretches, while overhead cables form a dense web between structures, at places almost obscuring their facades.“We stay here mainly because our coaching classes are close by. The lanes are congested and there are wires hanging everywhere, but what choice do we have? This is what fits my budget. If I look for a better or more spacious place, the rent goes up considerably, and as a student, I simply cannot afford that,” said Anamika, a student living in Shakurpur.In several properties, rooms have been carved out of packed buildings, leaving little room for ventilation or movement. “A double-sharing room starts at Rs 10,000 and can go up to Rs 14,000,” said an employee at a PG facility in Laxmi Nagar. The lane outside was dug up, forcing students to navigate an uneven stretch.The worry is visible closer to North Campus too. In Mukherjee Nagar, another major hub for students and competitive exam aspirants, electric poles and walls are plastered with boards offering rooms, phone numbers to call and promises of “Hi-Fi” facilities.From the road, it is not always obvious which buildings are being used as PGs. The reality becomes clear only after going upstairs. At one such building, cracked walls, dim staircases, exposed wires and electricity meters greet one at the entrance.“The condition is bad at many PGs, including mine, especially for the rent we pay. It is Rs 10,000-15,000 per person in a double-sharing room. If there is an emergency, it would be very difficult to rescue people,” said Devyani, who lives in Mukherjee Nagar. “But we don’t have many options, given it is closer to the campus.”In Guru Mandi, Vijay Nagar, getting to some PGs is a squeeze in itself. Narrow lanes are packed tight with houses. At one place, a cramped staircase takes you past the landlord’s portion before another flight leads up to the PG rooms. There are no visible fire extinguishers, and barely any ventilation.Students alleged several residential buildings are being used as PGs or for commercial accommodation, raising questions about whether adequate fire safety and other measures are in place.“I pay Rs 16,000 for a room on double sharing. The room is so small. Thankfully, I have a balcony, but not all rooms have that. These are residential buildings but are being run commercially without the necessary permissions. That means safety measures are often missing,” said Sukriti.Amen, who lives in Vijay Nagar, said the condition of some buildings was “frightening”. “When I hit my wall, it feels like it is moving. It is really scary,” he said. For Yashi, the nearby pocket of Malka Ganj is “much worse”.Apart from the lack of basic safety clearances and measures, the narrow lanes raise a bigger worry -- if something goes wrong, how quickly can students get out, and can emergency teams get in?The concern is not hypothetical. In 2023, a fire at a Mukherjee Nagar coaching centre trapped several students, who smashed windows and escaped using ropes, wires and pipes. In April, a transformer fire in Laxmi Nagar spread to a residential building, gutting 14 flats and forcing nearly 50 people to flee. Firefighters struggled to reach the site because of narrow, excavated roads.Across these student hubs, the issue goes beyond rent or room size. Thousands come to Delhi for college or coaching, but packed residential buildings, commercial PGs and congested lanes can turn even a small emergency into a serious safety risk.
Article Summary: In Delhi’s student hubs, finding a PG accommodation can mean squeezing through cramped lanes and narrow staircases in tightly-packed buildings. “PG available” signs compete with tangled wires and exposed meters. In some pockets, dug-up approach roads and poor ventilation add to the worry.

Article Title: Aspiring CA, 18, dies in Delhi PG collapse hours after Rakhi at home in MP; family donates corneas
Article Text:
In photo: Akshat Yadav (18), A building collapse in Delhi's Satya Niketan tragically ended the lives of several young students

Akshat Yadav

(18)

Yuvraj Soni

(20)

Arpit Jaj

(18)

Pawan Kumar

(17)





A mole on his neck and a mark left by a surgery on his right leg helped Akshat’s mother Sweta identify his body at AIIMS Monday.Akshat dreamt of becoming an IAS officer and making his parents proud. However, the dream was crushed beneath the rubble of the collapsed Satya Niketan building when the body of the second-year BCom (Hons) student at PGDAV College was pulled out at 7 am Monday.Akshat had been living in Delhi for the past two years and was a boarder at the PG accommodation for nearly a year. He lived on the first floor of the building and paid Rs 18,000 a month as rent. He returned to the city from his hometown in MP just two days before the incident after celebrating Raksha Bandhan.His cousin, Deepankar, who helped him find the accommodation, said, “I told Akshat to shift to Mayur Vihar, but he did not. He told me that it was only a matter of one year and that it would easily pass,” Deepankar said.Akshat’s family rushed to the spot after learning about the collapse. Just hours before the tragedy, on Sunday morning, Akshat had spoken to his parents over a video call. “Everything was fine,” Deepankar said.Hours later, the family was desperately searching for him in the rubble. Akshat’s wallet was found at the spot, helping the family establish that he was among those trapped in the debris. His body was later identified at AIIMS mortuary.His neighbour, Vijay Kumar Rajak, said Akshat was good at studies. “He mostly kept to himself and focused on his studies,” Rajak said.At AIIMS, Akshat’s younger sister wept inconsolably as the family struggled to come to terms with the loss of a young man whose ambitions and dreams were cut short.For Yuvraj’s relatives, the tragedy came as a double blow. Not only did they lose him, but his father, Kanhaiya, had to be hospitalised after being told that his son was critical. The family has not yet told Kanhiaya, who runs a medical store in Chhattisgarh, that Yuvraj is no more, fearing that the news is likely to worsen his condition.Yuvraj was speaking to his friend Gunjan on the phone when the building collapsed. The call suddenly disconnected, and Gunjan received no response despite repeatedly trying to contact him.A native of Chhattisgarh, Yuvraj was a BCom (Hons) student at Motilal Nehru College and was known to his friends and acquaintances as quiet and studious. He shifted to the fourth floor of the PG accommodation just a week before tragedy struck Sunday, his cousin said.On receiving information about the building collapse, Yuvraj’s relatives rushed to Delhi and waited anxiously as rescue teams cleared the debris. Through the long hours of the search, they continued to hope that Yuvraj would survive. Their hope, however, was dashed when his body was pulled out.Arpit’s family has decided to donate his corneas, hoping that even in death, he could help someone else regain their sight.The second-year BCom student, who aspired to become a chartered accountant, returned to his PG at 8am Sunday after celebrating Raksha Bandhan and Janmashtami with his family in MP’s Dewas, his friend Mayank said. Just a few hours later, the building turned into a death trap.Initially, Arpit’s family believed he was asleep when his mother’s calls went unanswered. Later, the family was informed about the incident and rushed to the spot, but it was all over by then. His body was identified at 6 pm.Arpit’s mother was seen weeping inconsolably at AIIMS, repeatedly asking why no one stopped him from returning to Delhi.A last-minute change in plans proved fatal for this native of UP’s Auraiya. Pawan had planned to visit his cousin Saturday and stay there till Sunday, but decided against. Hours later, he was trapped in the collapsed building.Pawan, who has four sister, was pursuing computer science with mathematics at Motilal Nehru College. His father is a retired veterinary doctor. His cousin, Dhiraj, said the PG was in a dilapidated condition.As soon as Pawan’s relatives heard about the collapse, they rushed to the spot and waited anxiously as rescue teams searched through the rubble. For several hours, they held onto the hope that he had survived as people at the site told them that some trapped residents had been rescued. “Many people said Pawan had been rescued and he was alive,” Dhiraj said.The family continued waiting for confirmation, clinging to every piece of information coming from the rescue site. Just after 10pm, their hopes were dashed when they learnt that Pawan had died. At the hospital, his father looked devastated, struggling to come to terms with the catastrophic loss.
Article Summary: Akshat Yadav dreamt of becoming an IAS officer and making his parents proud. Yuvraj Soni was speaking to his friend Gunjan on the phone when the building collapsed. Arpit Jaj's family decided to donate his corneas, hoping that even in death, he could help someone else regain their sight.

Article Title: Body parts of woman, child found in sacks in Keralam; missing husband’s role in murder suspected
Article Text:
Police said cattle herders spotted the sacks and alerted the Pudur police after noticing a strong stench emanating from them, raising their suspicion (AI Image)

(With agency inputs)





PALAKKAD: Police said the woman and child whose body parts were found in sacks in the Bhavani river a day ago have been identified.The murder suspect is believed to be the woman’s husband, a native of West Bengal, news agency PTI reported.A senior police officer leading the investigation said that family members of the victims are being contacted for a "full identification" of the remains.He further said the woman’s missing husband is suspected to be the culprit, and a team has been sent to trace and arrest him."The investigation is going on," he added.The body parts of the woman and child were found stuffed in two sacks abandoned on a dried-up portion of the Bhavani river near Cherakadav in Agali on Sunday.Police said cattle herders spotted the sacks and alerted the Pudur police after noticing a strong stench emanating from them, raising their suspicion.The body parts were in an advanced stage of decomposition, making identification difficult, police had said.

Police said cattle herders spotted the sacks and alerted the Pudur police after noticing a strong stench emanating from them.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.
