But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old techie fell into a trap by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal's combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Jains begin Paryushan from today
Article Text: Mumbai: Jain homes across the world will adopt a quieter, inward-looking rhythm from Tuesday as Paryushan Maha Parva begins. The eight-day festival focuses on fasting, self-reflection and forgiveness. This year, 1,065 Jains in Mulund have begun a month-long atthai fast, which will end on the festival's final day. The festival assumes added significance as the three Jain sects, Swetambars, Sthanakwasis and Terapanthis, will observe it together. Jain philosophy teacher Babulal Jain said fasting helps devotees overcome attachment, anger, greed and desire and attain inner peace. Around 500 Jain families in Japan are also expected to observe the fast. Across Mumbai, temples will hold scripture sessions. At NSCI Dome in Worli, Shrimad Rajchandra Mission will host programmes featuring Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji, while Parasdham will hold sessions led by Pujya Namramuniji.tnn
Article Summary: Eight-day festival focuses on fasting, self-reflection and forgiveness. 1,065 Jains in Mulund have begun a month-long atthai fast, which will end on festival's final day. Around 500 Jain families in Japan are also expected to observe the fast.

Article Title: Immersion tank trumps games at Dahisar school
Article Text: MUMBAI: Just days before a critical district sports competition, the playground of MPS Sakharam Tare Marg Municipal School in Dahisar has been dug up to construct an artificial Ganesh visarjan tank, leaving student-athletes without a place to train.The timing could not be worse for the school's 2,500 students. The upcoming event serves as a gateway for young sports talent, offering long-term opportunities for scholarships, sponsorships and academic incentives. Making matters worse, the 9,000 sq ft ground -- nestled between two school buildings -- was already constrained, with 30% of the area occupied by construction debris from ongoing work on one of the buildings.The Mumbai Suburban District sports competition features over 70 disciplines, including football, cricket, basketball, lawn tennis and boxing. "The competition is vital for students. Qualifying earns extra marks in board exams, helping them devote more time to sports," said Darshana Raut, the school's physical training teacher. "The pond was excavated without consulting the school. A similar setup last year took BMC a month to clear, leaving behind a mosquito-infested hazard.School administrative officer Asmita Kosle said complaints have been lodged. "There is definitely a safety risk to the children."Responding to the backlash, R-North ward officer Rohit Trivedi defended the site selection while promising swift action. "This particular site was chosen because it was on a list of approved sites from last year," he said. "For students' practice, we will make sure they are assigned a place in a nearby ground, and within three days from the last day of Ganesh Utsav, we will completely clear the ground."Deputy municipal commissioner (education) Prachi Jambhekar said, "I have instructed that the area has a 24-hour guard and is isolated from the students."
Article Summary: MPS Sakharam Tare Marg Municipal School in Dahisar has been dug up to construct an artificial Ganesh visarjan tank. The timing could not be worse for the school's 2,500 students. The upcoming event serves as a gateway for young sports talent, offering long-term opportunities.

Article Title: Woman held for stealing Rs 6.3 lakh jewellery from shop in five-star hotel
Article Text:
Mumbai:





A 49-year-old woman from Gujarat has been arrested for allegedly stealing jewellery worth Rs 6.3 lakh from a shop at the Oberoi Hotel in Nariman Point after posing as a customer and trying on several ornaments. After she left, the jeweller checked and found one pair of earrings worth Rs 2 lakh missing and on careful observation of the CCTV footage she was caught.The police arrested Priti Dasani, a resident of Porbandar district, Gujarat. Dasani was remanded in police custody.According to the police, the complainant, a 31-year-old employee of Vipul Arts Shop at Oberoi Hotel at Nariman Point, was attending to customers at the jewellery outlet on September 2. “Around 1 pm, the well-dressed Dasani entered the shop claiming that she wanted to purchase jewellery. She reportedly tried several gold ornaments, including rings, earrings, bracelets and bangles, for a considerable period before leaving without making a purchase,’’ said an official.After she left, the employee of the shop counted the jewellery and noticed that a pair of gold earrings, a ring and a single earring were missing.The shop employee informed the owner and checked footage recorded on his mobile phone. The footage showed the woman secretly placing jewellery in her trouser pocket while examining the ornaments. Based on the CCTV footage, the police registered an offence and started looking for her.During the investigation, police received information that the suspect was staying at a hotel in Kandivli (West). A team went to the hotel and found Dasani and arrested her. Police said the search of her belongings allegedly led to the recovery of a diamond-studded yellow-metal earring and Rs 2 lakh in cash, with the total seized property valued at around Rs 4 lakh. Police said the woman allegedly told investigators that she had sold some of the stolen jewellery at a shop in Zaveri Bazaar but gave vague details.
Article Summary: A 49-year-old woman from Gujarat has been arrested for allegedly stealing jewellery worth Rs 6.3 lakh from a shop at the Oberoi Hotel in Nariman Point. Priti Dasani, a resident of Porbandar district, Gujarat, was remanded in police custody.

CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange’s health deteriorated on the ninth day of his indefinite hunger strike at Antarwali Sarati on Sunday after he again refused medical treatment and stopped water intake. This has triggered anxiety among supporters and raised the possibility of shutdowns and road blockades in parts of Marathwada.A govt medical team made two attempts to examine Jarange between midnight and Sunday morning, but returned without providing treatment after he refused health checks and intravenous fluids. He had briefly resumed intake of water and fluids on Sept 2 following discussions with govt representatives.Addressing reporters, Jarange accused state govt of delaying a resolution to the Maratha reservation issue. “Govt offered Kunbi certificates but at the same time ensured they get cancelled too,” he said.The activist has set a Sept 11 deadline for govt to act on his demands, including the issuance of Kunbi certificates to eligible Marathas and a smoother process for granting validity certificates.As reports of his declining health spread, concern mounted among protesters gathered at the village.
Article Summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange’s health deteriorated on the ninth day of his indefinite hunger strike at Antarwali Sarati. He again refused medical treatment and stopped water intake. This has triggered anxiety among supporters and raised the possibility of shutdowns and road blockades in parts of Marathwada.

Article Title: Cops probe attacks on MSEDCL staff, RTI activist
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





The police are investigating two separate incidents -- an assault on MSEDCL employees in Rukadi and an attack on Right to Information activist Ashok Khade in Hupari, Kolhapur district.In the Rukadi case, a complaint was filed by MSEDCL junior engineer Ashraf Mulla, leading to a case being registered at Hatkanagale police station against four men — all residents of Vardhaman Nagar in Rukadi.According to the complaint, at around 9.30am on Sunday, MSEDCL employees visited a consumer’s house in Vardhaman Nagar to install a smart meter and check for electricity theft.There the team was allegedly abused, assaulted and pushed, and their official work was obstructed. The police have registered the matter as obstruction of govt duty.Ganpat Latpatte, superintending engineer of MSEDCL (Kolhapur division), said, “The power utility employees did not require any consent from the consumers to install smart meters or inspect premises for electricity theft. The smart meters are in the interest of the consumers and they are requested to cooperate.”In the second incident, four unidentified assailants on two motorcycles allegedly attacked Khade with wooden sticks while he was taking his usual evening walk on Karadga Road on Sunday evening. A case was registered with Hupari police station.Khade was taken in the vehicle to a private hospital and later shifted to CPR Hospital in Kolhapur for further treatment.Hupari police are examining CCTV footage to identify the attackers and investigating the motive.
Article Summary: MSEDCL employees visited a consumer’s house in Vardhaman Nagar to install a smart meter and check for electricity theft. There the team was allegedly abused, assaulted and pushed, and their official work was obstructed. In the second incident, four unidentified assailants on two motorcycles allegedly attacked Right to Information activist Ashok Khade with wooden sticks.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.

Article Title: 12-year-old girl, young woman rescued from prostitution racket in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Cops can be seen walking with 2 women. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued a 12-year-old girl and a 26-year-old woman from a prostitution racket being carried out at a lodge in Nerul after conducting a raid by sending a decoy customer on Thursday.The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers by providing them rooms at Kohinoor Palace Lodging and Boarding in Shiravane village, Nerul.Gajanan Kadam, AHTU senior inspector, said the rescued minor girl hails from UP and resided in Shiravane village with her cousins, who had brought her from UP after telling her parents that she would be given a job.The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours after booking a room. The accused demanded Rs 4,000 for supplying a woman.After the accused accepted the amount, the decoy customer signalled the police team waiting outside the lodge, following which they raided the premises.Inspector Kadam said, “The arrested accused are the lodge managers identified as Hridaykumar Singh and Deepak Ramrakhiani and the waiter Kuleshwar Kumar Singh.”At Nerul police station, an FIR was registered against the arrested accused by invoking BNS sections for trafficking of persons and joint criminal liability, along with the POCSO Act, which defines punishment for abetment, such as helping, encouraging or plotting any sexual crime against a child, and the Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act.On Friday, the three accused were produced before the Belapur JMFC court, which remanded them to police custody till Sept 9.
Article Summary: The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers. The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours.

Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Teen murdered, body dumped near Mini Seashore
Article Text:
A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi





NAVI MUMBAI: A 19-year-old boy was murdered and his body was dumped on the pavement near a public garden along Mini Seashore Road in Sector 10A, Vashi, early on Saturday morning. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused.Shashikant Chandekar, senior inspector of Vashi police station, said, "The murder victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane. A passing pedestrian spotted him lying unconscious in a pool of blood on the pavement around 4am. The pedestrian alerted Vashi police station, and our police team reached the spot and took the teenager to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead due to severe blood loss from grievous injuries to his head and wrist after being assaulted with some sharp lethal weapon. The victim Mahato hails from Bihar and resided with his father, who is an auto-rickshaw driver, his mother and two minor siblings. He worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and used to drive his father's auto-rickshaw during the night."Inspector Chandekar added, "Mahato had left home on Friday around 9pm, telling his mother that he was going to work at the Chinese food stall and was taking his father's auto-rickshaw to ferry passengers throughout the night.After his body was found early on Saturday morning, his family was informed. His father's auto-rickshaw was not found at the crime scene. Hence, it is suspected that after fatally assaulting Mahato, the assailant took away the auto-rickshaw, which is being traced by scanning CCTV footage along the route from Koparkhairane to Vashi."As there is no CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we are scanning CCTV footage from roads leading to the crime spot where Mahato's body was dumped to zero in on the suspect. Mahato might have been fatally assaulted at the spot, or he might have been assaulted at another location and his body brought in a vehicle and dumped near Mini Seashore. Accordingly, using technical expertise, efforts are being made to detect the murder case. Meanwhile, Mahato's kin and friends are being questioned to get some lead on the unidentified accused."
Article Summary: A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused. The victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane.

Article Title: 3 youths treckking to Chanderi fort near Panvel miss way, get stranded; rescued by cops
Article Text:
The rescued youths aged 22-25 years were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan.





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way and got stranded before being rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday.Gajanan Ghadge, Senior Inspector of Panvel Taluka Police Station, said that the rescued youths, aged between 22 and 25 years, were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan. They had started their trek at around 8 am.At around 11 am, the police helpline number 112 received a distress call from one of the trekkers, informing officials that they had lost their way while trekking towards Chanderi Fort."Upon receiving the information, we contacted the caller and asked him to share his live Google location. Accordingly, our police team, along with the Wavanje check-post beat marshal, Ritghar village head Deepak Patil, and the rescue team of NGO Sahyadri Pratishthan, launched a search operation by tracking the youth's mobile location," Ghadge said.The three youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.
Article Summary: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way. They were rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday. The youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai road rage: Ola driver attacked with stick, dragged 2km on car bonnet
Article Text:
The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a road rage incident in Nerul after an argument between the drivers of an Ola cab and a Swift car as the latter claimed that the Ola cab driver had dangerously cut his way while overtaking on the internal road in Nerul on August 15 night, the Swift car driver assaulted the cab driver by punching on his nose and hitting on the head with a bamboo stick causing him severe injuries.As the cab driver bled profusely and attempted to stop the car driver from getting away till the cops arrived, by lying on the car's bonnet, the car driver drove with the cab driver on the bonnet for about 2 kms.The cab driver while recording the incident on his mobile in one hand and firmly holding the bonnet by other hand, shouted for help from passing motorists, while dangling dangerously and requesting the car driver to stop by yelling that he could fall and get killed.As the car slowed down after some distance, the cab driver jumped off the bonnet after which the car driver sped away leaving the cab driver injured on the road.The incident occured on the stretch in sector 20 near Nerul pond on August 15 around 9.35pm.Ajay Kamble, senior inspector of Nerul said, "As per the complaint by the injured cab driver identified as Pradeepkumar Pandey, 27, a resident of Naigaon (E), an FIR was registered at Nerul police station against the unidentified accused car driver, who is absconding.From the Swift car's registration number provided by the complainant, the accused driver was identified as Lalit Arjun Patil, a resident of Juinagar. ""We have invoked relevant BNS sections for the offences of voluntarily causing hurt/ grievous hurt using dangerous weapons or means, voluntarily causing simple hurt, rash or negligent driving on a public way in a manner that endangers human life or is likely to cause hurt or injury to any person and causing simple hurt to any person through a rash or negligent act that endangers human life or personal safety," inspector Kamble added.As per the FIR, on August 15 at 8.18pm, the complainant Pandey had picked up two women passengers from Andheri and dropped them at Seawoods Grand Central mall in Nerul at around 9.30pm.Thereafter, he headed towards Sarsole to attend birthday party of his cousin Nitin Pandey's brother-in-law Rahul Chaubey.Around 9.35pm, when he reached near Nerul pond in sector 20, suddenly a Swift car driver was repeatedly honking. Hence, he changed the lane and gave him way to go ahead.But, the car driver waylaid him and alighting from his car claimed that he had dangerously cut his way while overtaking and punched on his nose, while hurling expletives.As the complainant tried to convince him and told not to give bad words, the car driver went to his vehicle and taking out a bamboo stick, hit on his head causing severe bleeding.As the assailant sat in his car, the complainant tried to stop him, but he started his car. Hence, the complainant lied on the car's bonnet to prevent him from escaping till the cops arrived.The assailant drove with the complainant on the bonnet for about 2kms, reluctant to stop the car.After some distance, as the car slowed down, he jumped off the bonnet and the assailant sped away.The complainant returned to his cab and called his cousin Dipanshu Pandey, who took him to NMMC's Meenatai Thackeray hospital, Nerul.The doctors gave him first aid and for further treatment referred him to NMMC hospital in Vashi, where he was administered sutures to head injury, followed by CT scan.Thereafter, he lodged a police complaint.
Article Summary: The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm. The Swift car driver assaulted the cab driver by punching on his nose and hitting on the head with a bamboo stick causing him severe injuries. The cab driver attempted to stop the car driver from getting away till the cops arrived, by lying on the car's bonnet.

Article Title: Four arrested for robbing MSRTC bus conductor of Rs 9,000 near Shirur
Article Text:
Pune:





The Pune Rural police on Sunday arrested four men for allegedly robbing an MSRTC bus conductor of Rs 9,000 in the early hours of Friday on the Pune-Nagar highway near Shirur, around 70km from the city.A Shirur police team led by inspector Vinod Patil arrested Ajaykumar Chavan (24) and Sachin Gholap (22), both from Dighi, and Pavan Gholap (25) and Akash Kale (21), both from Alandi, after examining footage from more than 100 CCTV cameras in Pimpri Chinchwad, Shirur and Ahilyanagar district.A state transport bus driver lodged a police complaint in this regard.An officer from the Shirur police said around 2am on Friday, the complainant was driving the bus towards Shirur bus depot when an SUV blocked his way. “Four men got out of the SUV and started abusing him, claiming that the bus had brushed against their vehicle. They also demanded money for the damage allegedly caused by the bus,” he said.“The complainant refuted their claim and told them to come along with him to the depot, where the mechanics would check the bus. He also assured them that he would pay if there were any damages,” the officer said.The accused, however, did not listen to the driver and began beating him up. When the bus conductor came to the driver’s help, the accused assaulted him too and robbed him of Rs 9,000. “Before leaving the spot, the accused smashed the windscreen of the bus by pelting stones and took away the keys of the vehicle,” the officer said.Police have seized the SUV allegedly used in the crime.
Article Summary: Pune Rural police on Sunday arrested four men for allegedly robbing an MSRTC bus conductor of Rs 9,000. The incident took place on the Pune-Nagar highway near Shirur, around 70km from the city. A state transport bus driver lodged a police complaint in this regard. Police have seized the SUV allegedly used in the crime.

Article Title: Extra checks for electors over 25 years of age filling voter enrolment form
Article Text:
Voters checking the electoral roll

Pune:

TOI





Voters over 25 years seeking inclusion in the electoral roll will face additional scrutiny. Electoral officials have been directed to verify their previous enrolment details and residential addresses before deciding their claims, state chief electoral officer toldon Monday.The directions were issued by his office while officials were told how they could dispose of claims and objections received during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.Applicants above 25 years of age will have to provide their full residential address and EPIC number and officials will run checks against the electoral rolls to ascertain whether the applicant is enrolled elsewhere.If that is the case, officials will inform the person that multiple enrolment is against the law and advise them to delete their name from one location.The directive also specifically deals with voters in the absent, shifted, dead, duplicate and others category. Such voters can submit Form 6 to seek inclusion. Such voters will have to only provide their EPIC to check their status.Officials will check ASDDO voters’ previous electoral roll entry and EPIC details. If the voter’s name is found in the roll elsewhere, the claim will be dealt with accordingly and the voter will not be in more than one location.The directions come as electoral authorities begin looking at claims and objections filed after the publication of the draft rolls under SIR. Claims cannot be disposed of mechanically and registration officers can ask claimants or objectors to appear personally and seek evidence where necessary.The CEO’s office has told officials to ensure that applications for inclusion, correction and deletion are well scrutinised, especially in cases involving discrepancies in mapping and previous electoral records.The focus on voters above 25 is significant as it means a person seeking first-time inclusion at an older age is likely to undergo a more detailed check of their electoral history, rather than simply being added to the roll on the basis of the claim, officials added.Applicants seeking inclusion should provide the declaration and supporting details, while officials must ensure that the final electoral roll is accurate and free of duplicate entries, the orders said.
Article Summary: Voters over 25 years seeking inclusion in the electoral roll will face additional scrutiny. Officials will run checks against the electoral rolls to ascertain whether the applicant is enrolled elsewhere. If that is the case, officials will inform the person that multiple enrolment is against the law and advise them to delete their name.

Article Title: Four trips of Nagpur-Pune Exp cancelled
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Central Railway has cancelled four trips of Nagpur-Pune and Pune-Nagpur Express trains due to Pre-Non-Interlocking (Pre-NI) and Non-Interlocking (NI) works at Pune and Hadapsar yards.Train No. 12114 Nagpur-Pune Express will be cancelled on Oct 2, while Train No. 12113 Pune-Nagpur Express will remain cancelled on Oct 3.Train No. 12136 Nagpur-Pune Express will also be cancelled on Oct 3, followed by Train No. 12135 Pune-Nagpur Express on Oct 4. In addition, Train No. 12135 Pune-Nagpur Express will be diverted on Sept 20. It will run via Pune-Lonavala-Karjat-Panvel-Kalyan-Igatpuri-Manmad instead of its usual route.Railway authorities have advised passengers to take note of the changes and check the status of their trains before commencing their journey.
Article Summary: Central Railway has cancelled four trips of Nagpur-Pune and Pune-Nagpur Express trains. This is due to Pre-Non-Interlocking (Pre-NI) and Non-Inter locking (NI) works at Pune and Hadapsar yards. Train No. 12135 Pune - Nagpur Express will be diverted on Sept 20.
